root_cause.text: The dpaa2-switch IRQ handler introduced an error path for out-of-range if_id values that exited before calling dpsw_clear_irq_status(), leaving the interrupt pending and causing repeated IRQ retriggering.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the invalid-if_id branch in dpaa2_switch_irq0_handler_thread() from `goto out;` to `goto out_clear;`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that after commit 31a7a0bbeb00, “If an out-of-bounds if_id is detected, the interrupt status is not cleared. This may result in an interrupt storm.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The dpaa2-switch IRQ handler introduced an error path for out-of-range if_id values that exited before calling dpsw_clear_irq_status(), leaving the interrupt pending and causing repeated IRQ retriggering.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the invalid-if_id branch in dpaa2_switch_irq0_handler_thread() from `goto out;` to `goto out_clear;`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that after commit 31a7a0bbeb00, “If an out-of-bounds if_id is detected, the interrupt status is not cleared. This may result in an interrupt storm.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix invalid interface ID interrupt handling by taking the interrupt-clear exit path instead of returning without clearing the condition.
intent_record.what: The error path for the condition where if_id is greater than or equal to ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs was changed from jumping to the label out to jumping to the label out_clear after logging "Invalid if_id %d in IRQ status".
intent_record.how: At runtime, when an interrupt reports an invalid interface ID, execution now follows the cleanup path associated with out_clear instead of the plain exit path, which likely ensures the interrupt status or related condition is cleared before returning and prevents the same invalid interrupt condition from persisting or retriggering.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a branch target before IRQ status clearing so error or early-exit paths can still acknowledge the interrupt correctly.
intent_record.what: A new label named "out_clear:" was inserted immediately before the call to dpsw_clear_irq_status() in dpaa2_switch_irq0_handler_thread().
intent_record.how: This provides a jump target so execution can branch directly to the IRQ status clearing code from elsewhere in the function, ensuring the interrupt status can still be acknowledged on those paths.

grouping_result.intent: Add a branch target before IRQ status clearing so error or early-exit paths can still acknowledge the interrupt correctly.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure all error or early-exit interrupt handling paths still reach the IRQ status clearing logic so invalid conditions are acknowledged correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: they reroute invalid/out-of-range interface ID error handling to the interrupt-status clearing path instead of returning early, ensuring dpsw_clear_irq_status() is still called and preventing repeated IRQ retriggering.

candidates.rationale: This early exit on invalid if_id bypasses the later dpsw_clear_irq_status() call, leaving the interrupt pending and causing retriggering.
This conditional introduces the invalid-if_id error path; combined with the goto out branch, it causes the handler to exit before acknowledging the IRQ.

vuln_statements.explanation: This branch is taken on an out-of-range if_id and exits via the out label before the later dpsw_clear_irq_status() acknowledgment path, leaving the interrupt pending and causing repeated IRQ retriggering.
This conditional creates the invalid-if_id error path that triggers the early exit. In combination with the goto out statement, it causes the handler to leave without clearing IRQ status.

The function now adds `if (if_id >= ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs) { dev_err(dev, "Invalid if_id %d in IRQ status\n", if_id); goto out; }` immediately after extracting `if_id = (status & 0xFFFF0000) >> 16;`.
